specifics.why_no_category_fits: The two duplicated members are SwiftUI `body` computed properties on concrete `View`-conforming structs (`SmallNowPlayingWidgetEntryView` and `MediumNowPlayingWidgetEntryView`). The idiomatic Swift/SwiftUI remedy is view composition — extracting a shared child `View` struct — rather than any of the named categories. `extract-to-common` does not apply because both files already live in the same package (`app:iOS`) and the same directory; there is no cross-package extraction needed. `generic-parameterization` does not apply because the variation is in layout constants, not in generic type parameters. `default-implementation` does not apply because `body` is a protocol requirement of `View` whose default cannot be meaningfully shared across unrelated concrete types without coupling them. `subclass-lift` does not apply because SwiftUI views are structs, not classes. The closest named category would be `composition`, but the schema for `composition` models the case where one type becomes a *field* of another, whereas here the goal is to introduce a *third* extracted view type composed into both existing views — a three-way relationship the `composition` schema does not capture cleanly.
